name: Dan Green
current_role: U.S. Navy officer and former Pentagon official
bio: Dan Green is a U.S. Navy commander who joined the Navy after working at the Pentagon on September 11, 2001, and deployed to Iraq and Afghanistan, including with SEAL teams. He also served a civilian State Department tour in Afghanistan and was Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Strategy and Force Development. He is the Republican nominee for Florida's 9th District.

platform.point: Keep the military well funded and ready.
Bring down homeowners insurance rates for Floridians.
Lower grocery, gas and fuel prices by reversing Biden administration policies.
Address overdevelopment pressures on Central Florida communities.
Use conservative approaches to make homeownership affordable again.
Protect constitutional government and individual freedoms.

foreign.evidence: Campaign pledges to maintain strong military funding and readiness, drawing on his counterterrorism and foreign policy work.

photo.author: JoAnne Sorrentino, U.S. Department of Defense

notes: Campaign site lists priorities without detailed policy specifics.

name: Maxwell Frost
bio: Maxwell Frost has represented Florida's 10th District since 2023 and serves on the Oversight and Science, Space, and Technology committees. Born in Orlando, he attended Valencia College and worked as an organizer, including as national organizing director for March for Our Lives and with the ACLU.

platform.point: Make ending gun violence a top priority.
Pursue Medicare for All.
Overhaul the criminal justice system.
Act to end the climate crisis, including a Green New Deal.
Expand abortion access, including ending the Hyde Amendment.
Refuses corporate PAC contributions.

economy.evidence: Progressive Caucus member backing large public investment such as a Green New Deal and refusing corporate PAC money.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion access, cannabis and sex-work decriminalization, while backing strong gun control.

security.evidence: Advocates transforming criminal justice toward a future without prisons.

immigration.evidence: Opposes a southern border wall and has pressed for due process in detention oversight visits.

foreign.evidence: Opposed additional Israel military funding citing Gaza conduct, while backing a two-state solution.

energy.evidence: Backs a Green New Deal and environmental justice.

notes: Unopposed; the general election for this seat is canceled.

name: Joe Strada
bio: Joe Strada is a Central Florida businessman who started in the skilled trades and grew a family-owned company. He won the 2026 Republican nomination for Florida's 11th District after a recount.

platform.point: Investigate congressional insider trading.
Enact term limits for members of Congress.
Pass a balanced budget amendment and cut wasteful spending.
Secure the border and fight cartels and fentanyl.
Protect Social Security and Medicare.
Expand school choice and restore parental rights.

economy.evidence: Calls for slashing government spending and cutting burdensome regulations.

welfare.evidence: Pledges to protect Social Security and Medicare alongside spending cuts.

liberty.evidence: Defends constitutional (gun) rights but backs restricting women's sports to biological females.

security.evidence: Lists restoring law and order among priorities.

immigration.evidence: Priorities include securing the border and stopping cartels.

foreign.evidence: Backs peace through strength and standing up to China.

education.evidence: Supports expanding school choice and parental rights.

faith.evidence: Lists protecting religious liberty as a priority.

name: James Pericola
bio: James Pericola is a Central Florida native and attorney with over 30 years in public service and government affairs. He was a Clinton administration appointee at the National Transportation Safety Board and worked on the staff of Senator Bob Graham.

platform.point: End federal income tax for people earning under $100,000 and cut middle-class taxes.
Protect the Affordable Care Act and let Medicare negotiate drug prices.
Oppose cuts to or privatization of Social Security and Medicare.
Secure federal housing funds and lower property insurance costs.
End gerrymandering and pass the John Lewis Voting Rights Act.

economy.evidence: Proposes income-tax relief below $100,000 and Medicare drug-price negotiation.

welfare.evidence: Backs protecting the ACA, Social Security and Medicare from cuts.

name: Ralph Groves
current_role: Former chair, Libertarian Party of Orange County
bio: Ralph Groves recently chaired the Libertarian Party of Orange County, Florida. He served in Army and Defense Department roles in Germany, the United Kingdom, West Africa and Armenia, and holds a Doctor of Arts in history from St. John's University.

platform.point: Defend the individual right to bear arms, oppose gun-free zones and question the effectiveness of background checks.
Expects states to set abortion policy and opposes using taxpayer funds for abortion.
Describes himself as anti-war while supporting U.S. defense industries.
Supports safety courses for gun owners, similar to driver education.

liberty.evidence: Guns: opposes gun-free zones and doubts background checks work; abortion: expects states to set rules and opposes public funding.

foreign.evidence: Describes himself as anti-war while backing U.S. defense industries.

notes: Secondary coverage summarizes his abortion stance as leaving extreme cases to women and doctors, which differs from his position paper.

name: Gus Bilirakis
bio: Gus Bilirakis has served in the U.S. House since 2007, first for Florida's 9th District and since 2013 for the 12th, and chairs the Energy and Commerce subcommittee on innovation, data and commerce. He previously served in the Florida House from 1998 to 2006 and practiced as a probate and estate-planning attorney. He grew up in Tarpon Springs.

platform.point: Offer homeowners up to a $10,000 deduction through the Homeowners Premium Tax Reduction Act.
End taxes on tips, overtime and Social Security.
Fund cancer research and extend telehealth access for seniors.
Strengthen border security to stop fentanyl trafficking.
Protect children online, building on the Take It Down Act.
Support veteran housing and mental-health services.

economy.evidence: Voted for the 2017 tax cuts, signed the Taxpayer Protection Pledge and backs ending taxes on tips and overtime.

welfare.evidence: Has supported repealing the Affordable Care Act.

liberty.evidence: Holds an NRA A rating and backs concealed-carry reciprocity (guns).

security.evidence: Emphasizes school-safety funding and anti-fentanyl enforcement.

immigration.evidence: Campaigns on border security; voted for the Laken Riley Act.

foreign.evidence: Voted to support Israel after October 7 and co-signed a letter condemning Azerbaijan's Nagorno-Karabakh offensive.

energy.evidence: Signed a pledge against climate legislation that raises taxes.

tech.evidence: Backed the Take It Down Act and parental tools for kids' online safety.

name: Kimberly Overman
bio: Kimberly Overman served as an at-large Hillsborough County Commissioner from 2018 to 2022, including as chair. She is a retired certified financial planner and former small-business owner trained in economics. She moved her 2026 campaign from Florida's 15th District to the 12th after redistricting.

platform.point: Lower drug costs and expand coverage, especially mental health care.
Restore and protect abortion rights and reproductive care.
Invest in schools, raise teacher pay and expand early childhood and vocational education.
Pair law enforcement with mental health services and community crime prevention.
Increase investment in affordable housing and transportation.
Fund flood mitigation, drainage and clean water as climate resilience.

welfare.evidence: Calls for expanded health coverage and lower drug costs.

liberty.evidence: Supports restoring abortion rights (abortion is the only listed liberty issue on her current issues page).

security.evidence: Backs law enforcement combined with mental health and prevention programs.

education.evidence: Calls for stronger public school investment and teacher pay.

notes: LGBTQ and gun positions cited earlier were not found on her current issues page.

name: Branden Scrivener
bio: Branden Scrivener is running without party affiliation in Florida's 12th District. He holds a bachelor's degree in human services, has worked in healthcare for over three years, and interned with Catholic Charities and Tampa Crossroads on housing and counseling services.
notes: Very limited public information; no issue positions could be found.

name: Anna Paulina Luna
bio: Anna Paulina Luna has represented Florida's 13th District since 2023. She served in the U.S. Air Force from 2009 to 2014, earned a biology degree from the University of West Florida, and was director of Hispanic engagement at Turning Point USA. She was raised in Southern California.

platform.point: Oppose illegal immigration and support border wall efforts.
Oppose tech censorship and break up large tech firms.
Suspend further military aid to Ukraine.
Protect Second Amendment rights without new restrictions.
Cap credit card interest rates at 10 percent.

economy.evidence: Favors tax cuts and opposes stimulus spending, though co-sponsored a credit card interest cap.

welfare.evidence: Opposes expanding the Affordable Care Act.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion bans but opposes gun restrictions and vaccine mandates.

security.evidence: Supports qualified immunity and opposes defunding police.

immigration.evidence: Supported border wall initiatives and campaigns against illegal immigration.

foreign.evidence: Voted against the $60 billion Ukraine package and has opposed NATO membership.

energy.evidence: Favors prioritizing domestic oil production for U.S. use.

tech.evidence: Wants to break up Big Tech and rewrite FCC rules for social media.

education.evidence: Opposes teaching gender theory in schools.

faith.evidence: Says religious liberty is at risk and favors keeping God in public life.

notes: Tech score raised from 25 to 55 because she calls for breaking up Big Tech and new social media rules.

name: Leela Gray
bio: Leela Gray is a retired Army brigadier general who served more than 30 years, including as a communications officer working to counter terrorist propaganda. She holds degrees from Elon University, Ball State, the Army War College and Stetson law school. She won the 2026 Democratic primary for Florida's 13th District in her first run for office.

platform.point: Focus on rising living costs that working families cannot keep up with.
Take on insurance monopolies driving up premiums.
Support a middle-class tax cut.
Opposes Medicaid and SNAP cuts in the 2025 budget law.
Opposes the Trump administration's tariffs.

economy.evidence: Backs a middle-class tax cut and action against insurance monopolies while opposing tariffs.

welfare.evidence: Criticizes Medicaid and SNAP cuts in the 2025 budget law.

foreign.evidence: Opposes U.S. military action in Iran.

name: Tony D'Arrigo
bio: Tony D'Arrigo is a small-business owner with a background in hospitality management and a published author. He describes himself as a former Republican and is running without party affiliation in Florida's 13th District, refusing corporate PAC money.

platform.point: Expand coverage toward universal care, de-privatize hospitals and protect the ACA.
Protect Medicare and Medicaid and increase Social Security benefits.
Eliminate federal income tax for households earning under $75,000.
Promote affordable clean energy and electric vehicles.
Expand homeownership through government-backed mortgages.
Provide free school meals and child health care.

welfare.evidence: Calls health care his top issue, seeking expanded coverage and de-privatized hospitals.

energy.evidence: Campaign backs affordable clean energy and electric vehicles.

name: Kathy Castor
bio: Kathy Castor has served in the U.S. House since 2007 and chaired the Select Committee on the Climate Crisis from 2019 to 2023; she is ranking member of the Energy and Commerce energy subcommittee. She previously served on the Hillsborough County Commission from 2002 to 2006 and worked as a land-use attorney. She is from Tampa.

platform.point: Secure federal investment that creates local jobs.
Advance environmental protections and climate action.
Work to lower costs for families.
Protect the ACA and expand Medicaid coverage in Florida.
Ban assault weapons and fund gun violence research.

economy.evidence: Emphasizes federal investment to drive the local economy and jobs.

welfare.evidence: Supports the ACA and Medicaid expansion.

liberty.evidence: Backs abortion rights and same-sex marriage, alongside an assault weapons ban.

immigration.evidence: Supports a pathway to citizenship and legalization for Dreamers.

foreign.evidence: Backs Israel security aid and Iran sanctions but voted to repeal the 2002 Iraq war authorization.

energy.evidence: Chaired the climate crisis committee and wrote a broad climate action plan.

education.evidence: Opposes school vouchers and supports free community college.

notes: Security score (previously 30) set to null because no supporting evidence was found.
